record.original_question: Consider the elliptic equation Delta u = -V'_u(u, x1, ..., xn), where V is 1-periodic in u, x1, ..., xn. Suppose that for every rotation vector alpha in R^n there exists a foliation of T^(n+1) by graphs of minimal solutions of slope alpha. Does it follow that V does not depend on u?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 1$ and let $V:\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, $(u,x_1,\dots,x_n)\mapsto V(u,x_1,\dots,x_n)$, be a smooth function that is $1$-periodic in each of its $n+1$ arguments. Consider the elliptic Euler–Lagrange equation
$$\Delta u(x) \;=\; -\,\partial_u V\bigl(u(x),x_1,\dots,x_n\bigr), \qquad x=(x_1,\dots,x_n)\in\mathbb{R}^n,$$
associated to the variational integrand $\tfrac12|\nabla u|^2 - V(u,x_1,\dots,x_n)$. A function $u:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ is called a minimal solution if it is a smooth solution of the equation and minimizes the action on every compact set among compactly supported variations. Such a $u$ is said to have rotation vector (slope) $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}^n$ if $u(x)-\alpha\cdot x$ is bounded on $\mathbb{R}^n$. Identify $\mathbb{T}^{n+1}=\mathbb{R}^{n+1}/\mathbb{Z}^{n+1}$ in coordinates $(u,x_1,\dots,x_n)$.

Assume that for every rotation vector $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}^n$ there exists a foliation of $\mathbb{T}^{n+1}$ whose leaves are the graphs (projected to $\mathbb{T}^{n+1}$) of minimal solutions of slope $\alpha$.

Question: Does it follow that $V$ is independent of $u$, i.e. $\partial_u V\equiv 0$?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located the foundational works of Moser and Bangert on minimal foliations on tori and follow-up developments (Rabinowitz–Stredulinsky, de la Llave and others) and an example of nonexistence of minimal foliations, but no source was found that explicitly resolves the rigidity question of whether existence of a minimal foliation for every rotation vector forces the potential to be independent of $u$. The status appears unresolved in the literature accessible by search.

status_evidence.title: On minimal laminations of the torus
status_evidence.snippet: Bangert's theory of minimal solutions and laminations for variational problems on the torus.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational framework for the question; does not provide the rigidity claim.

status_evidence.title: Minimal foliations on a torus (Moser)
status_evidence.snippet: Moser's development of minimal foliations for elliptic variational problems on the torus.
status_evidence.claim: Sets up the context; does not answer the rigidity question.

status_evidence.title: An example for nonexistence of minimal foliations
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs potentials for which minimal foliations of certain slopes fail to exist.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the subtlety of the foliation hypothesis but does not answer the converse rigidity question.
